title: Leaf count identity for path erasure
statement: Let $P$ be a family of protocols indexed by bits, let $b$ be a bit, and let $s$ have a subprotocol path into $P(b)$. If $e=\ell(P(b))-\ell(s)+1$, with subtraction truncated on the natural numbers, then replacing the leaf count of branch $b$ by $e$ in the sum of the two branch leaf counts gives $\ell(P(\mathrm{false}))+\ell(P(\mathrm{true}))-\ell(s)+1$, again using truncated subtraction.
replaced:
Let $P$ assign a protocol to each bit, let $b$ be a bit, and let $s$ be a subprotocol of
$P(b)$ witnessed by a subprotocol path. If $e = \ell(P(b)) - \ell(s) + 1$ (truncated
subtraction on $\mathbb{N}$), then replacing the leaf count of branch $b$ by $e$ in the sum
of the two children's leaf counts gives
\[
  \ell(P(\mathrm{false})) + \ell(P(\mathrm{true})) - \ell(s) + 1 ,
\]
i.e.\ $\ell(P(\mathrm{false})) + e = \ell(P(\mathrm{false})) + \ell(P(\mathrm{true})) - \ell(s) + 1$
when $b = \mathrm{true}$, and $e + \ell(P(\mathrm{true}))$ equals the same quantity when
$b = \mathrm{false}$.
